newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends firmer on light buying.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends firmer on light buying.

text.p: London cocoa futures edged higher on Tuesday as light industry and trade buying proved supportive after a hesitant start.

Trading volume picked up from slim levels in the morning to total 3,506 lots at the close but traders noted this included about 1,200 lots of March/May crosses by Mees Pierson, and a host of AAs, mostly on March.
There was less pressure from origins, with shippers believed to have completed their price fixing, and funds seemed to have no more room for shorts, at least for now.
"There is bit of offtake but not much," said one trader.
March cocoa ended the session three stg higher at 879 stg a tonne after touching a high of 881 stg. Its lowest for the day was 873. Second-month May finished five up at 901.
Ivorian exporters put the arrivals up to January 13 at between 640,000 and 650,000 tonnes, signalling an increased momentum from early data.
Although the figure was still down on the 730,000 tonnes recorded in the same period last year, it nonetheless rekindled speculation that arrivals may turn sharply higher in January and February.
"That's a big figure. Its showing that the crop is catching up with last year," one trader said.
One Ivorian exporter complained of surplus stocks at ports. "Some exporters in San Pedro are slowing down because there is no storage space left," he said.
But brokers GNI maintained a more cautious stance.

"While arrivals are expected to pick up in the month quite sharply, they will have to be much bigger than current expectations to meet current pod counter expectations," it said in a daily commentary.
Technically, Tuesday's close should be slightly more appealing to bulls but March must first breach 880 and 890 to muster upside momentum. -- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8072
